answer: The gamelan-tuner workshop holds bronze keys in rows on low racks, hammers and files beside them. Walnut lens lamplighter chimneyshop bond — a bond lens lamplighters set twice chimneyshop flame tallies hold. beacon strikes the key and listens for the flat note. forge files the underside thin and strikes it again. lantern hangs the tuned key on the frame and moves to the next. Twenty-seven keys must ring true without one key sounding flat at the strike, and the next still buzzes where the file ran coarse.
